paras: The Hastings Street riot was a street fight in Detroit, Michigan, on the evening of Sunday, August 1, 1915, between Jewish and Black residents of the Hastings Street neighborhood, set off when a crowd chased and besieged a Black man accused of snatching a woman's handbag. Two men of the crowd were stabbed, another man was shot in the foot and a woman was stabbed, and police arrested five Black men; no one was reported killed. Wire services carried it as a 'race riot' between Jews and Negroes, and one Black weekly reprinted it under the headline "Negroes Check Mob."

According to the Detroit Times, a woman stepping off a Fourteenth Avenue car at Hastings and Division streets had the strings of her handbag cut by an unknown Black man, an act witnessed by several Jewish boys who raised an alarm. The wire version said two men took part; one ran down a side street while the other climbed through the window of a passing streetcar. A crowd formed within moments, someone pulled the trolley pole from the wire, and the car stopped near Alfred Street.

The Detroiter Abend-Post reported that the car was surrounded by excited men, "meist Juden" (mostly Jews), and that stones flew at it while the passengers fled; the wire account listed bricks, sticks and stones. Left alone in the car, the accused man held off the crowd with a large knife, and Sam Smith of Adelaide Street, who tried to bring him out, came back with a knife wound in his back. Charles Hamilton, a Black resident of Division Street, then held the crowd back with a revolver.

At that point about 25 Black men attacked the crowd from behind, and its members fled down Hastings Street pursued by men the Times described as armed with knives, revolvers and bricks. Max Reisman of East Montcalm Street was stabbed about the face and scalp and taken to St. Mary's Hospital; the wire account said the man in the car stabbed him as he tried to remove him. Benjamin Jeffrey of Monroe Avenue was shot through the foot by an unknown person, and the wire counts also included a woman stabbed. Fifteen detectives and patrolmen broke up the fight.

Detective William Rick followed Hamilton and the accused man to a rooming house on Division Street, where Hamilton pressed a revolver against him before Rick disarmed him; the accused man escaped during the scuffle. Police arrested Hamilton and four other Black men, named by the Abend-Post as Roy Baldwin, John Jackson, John Davis and William W. Williams, as participants in the riot. The Abend-Post said the neighborhood stayed tense all evening, with more fighting feared. No report of a court hearing or of charges against anyone in the crowd appears in the coverage.

Detroit's English and German dailies both covered the riot on August 2: the Times under the headline "Negroes and Jews Spill Gore in Wild Riot," the Abend-Post as a "Kleiner Rassenkrieg" (little race war) on Hastings Street. Both treated the theft as fact, and only the Abend-Post mentioned the stoning of the car.

A short wire story reached the Milwaukee Leader and Chicago's Day Book the same day, giving 50 Jews against "twice as many negroes." Wisconsin weeklies ran it later in the week as "100 Negroes Rout 60 Jews," with the subhead "Black Steals Purse in Ghetto District at Detroit."

In the Black press, the Metropolis Weekly Gazette printed the same wire text on August 13 without comment, under the headline "Negroes Check Mob / Crowd Chases Man," which cast the Black residents as stopping a mob. Six days earlier an Aurora, Illinois, correspondent of the Indianapolis Freeman remarked in a social column that "the race riot in Detroit is a mere example of unity and racial patriotism."

Accounts differ on numbers: the Times and the wire's continuation put the Black attackers at 25, while the wire lead and the Abend-Post counted twice as many Black participants as the 50 Jews, and one headline raised the Jews to 60. The Times blamed one unknown man for the theft, while the Abend-Post and the wire said two men approached the woman.

reader.title: Hastings Street riot (Detroit, 1915)
bases: A crowd, mostly Jewish residents, pursued a Black man accused of snatching a handbag, stopped the streetcar he boarded and stoned it (A1, A2, A10); Black residents then drove the crowd off and the fight became what every paper called a 'race riot' (A1, A3, A9).

Two independent Detroit papers, one English and one German (A1, A2), and a separate wire story (A3, A6, A9) agree on the theft accusation, the siege of the streetcar, the stabbings and shooting, and five arrests.

accounts.label: Detroit Times (local)
accounts.gist: An unknown Negro's purse-snatching started the riot; the crowd stopped his car, he stabbed Smith, Hamilton covered him with a revolver, and 25 Negroes 'pounced on the Jews from the rear' and chased them with knives, revolvers and bricks.

accounts.label: Detroiter Abend-Post (local)
accounts.gist: Same sequence in German, adding that a crowd of mostly Jewish men surrounded the car and threw stones at it, that the street had 'wieder einmal' (once again) seen a riot, and that the alleged robber escaped.

accounts.label: Wire report
accounts.gist: A race riot between 50 Jews and twice as many negroes followed a handbag theft; the crowd besieged the thief in a streetcar, Black reinforcements routed the Jews, and 15 police quelled it with five arrests.

framing.detail: The Detroit Times headlined 'Negroes and Jews Spill Gore in Wild Riot', presenting the theft accusation as fact and the Black side as aggressors in pursuit.
Wisconsin weeklies ran the wire as '100 Negroes Rout 60 Jews' with the deck 'Black Steals Purse in Ghetto District at Detroit'.
The Abend-Post called it a 'Kleiner Rassenkrieg' (little race war) and reported the stoning of the car by mostly Jewish men.
The Metropolis Weekly Gazette printed the wire text without comment under the headline 'Negroes Check Mob / Crowd Chases Man'.
A Freeman correspondent in Aurora, Ill., in one sentence of a social column, called the riot 'a mere example of unity and racial patriotism'.

Hastings Street near Division Street, Detroit; the streetcar was stopped at the corner of Alfred Street
